concept.name: Fibonacci extension
concept.definition: A charting technique that projects levels beyond the prior swing — conventionally 100%, 161.8%, and 261.8% of the measured move — as candidate profit-target or exhaustion zones once the trend resumes. Like retracements, it is an analytical convention, not a validated forecasting law.
concept.intuition: If the retracement yardstick measures how far price pulls back, the extension yardstick guesses how far the next leg might reach.
concept.mechanics: Applied after a trend resumes: the prior swing's range (or the swing plus its retracement, in three-point projection tools) is multiplied by extension ratios and projected past the old extreme. The 161.8% projection is the most widely watched target.
concept.formula: Extension level (up-move) = Low + e x (High - Low) with e > 1 (e.g., 1.618); three-point variant: target = RetracementLow + e x (High - Low).
concept.failure_modes: All the subjectivity of retracements applies, compounded by the choice of anchor points; trends frequently stop well short of, or blow through, projected extensions.
concept.misconceptions: That extension targets are high-probability exit prices; they are reference zones at best, and many moves never reach the 161.8% projection.
concept.example: After a stock rallies 40 to 50 and resumes upward from a 46 pullback, the 161.8% extension of the 40-50 leg projects a target zone near 62.2 (46 + 1.618 x 10).
